The supplied units are BASE-side text of EngineV2BridgeTests.swift, a test-only file, covering lines 677-1869. The patch changes add a decodeTable to StubTokenizer, a stopStringScope parameter on makeBridge, and new tests (head lines 811-896) for a scoped matched stop sequence via ModelEOSPolicy.stopStringScope. The visible patch excerpt is truncated, so the new tests are not fully visible.

The changes ship no production code. I found no new attack surface, no weakening of a trust boundary, and no change to key handling, attestation, authorization or cache storage.

Relevant base-side content is an existing test that the bridge stamps cacheSalt only from the coordinator-supplied cacheScope. Caller-controlled fields such as prompt_cache_key and user are ignored (lines 754-778). That matches the T-041 mitigation. It is unchanged by this PR and remains asserted.

The source behavior behind the new stopStringScope and matchedStopSequence(scope:) is not in the supplied evidence. It is the production change that the tests exercise, and it may sit in a different batch, e.g. EngineV2Bridge.swift or ModelEOSPolicy. The integration pass should check that the scoped stop-matching logic cannot leak reasoning or analysis-channel text to the consumer, or alter billing and usage accounting. I cannot judge that from these test units alone. No finding is raised, and the contract remains unverified in this batch.
